Chatbot Governance

Privacy, security, accuracy and accountability across enterprise LLM chatbots and AI agents.

Explore the presentation

Govern the full lifecycle

This presentation moves from the chatbot risk landscape to a layered governance framework, privacy practices, RAG checkpoints, agent permissions and an operating model. It concludes with monitoring, incident response and a proposed 90-day adoption plan.

Source edition: November 2026. Legal summaries, dates, framework versions and rankings are preserved from the source presentation and have not been independently verified in this conversion. Use the slides as source material, not a determination of applicable legal obligations.

Why Governance Matters

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance W H Y I T M AT T E R S Why chatbot governance matters now Liable Air Canada, Feb 2024 A tribunal held the airline responsible for its chatbot's wrong answer on bereavement fares: a chatbot is still part of your website. Aug 2, 2026 EU AI Act, Article 50 Chatbots must tell people they are talking to AI. Fines can reach €15M or 3% of worldwide turnover. #3 OWASP LLM Top 10, 2026 Excessive agency jumped to the third-biggest risk as chatbots gain tools and start taking actions. Governance is what lets you scale chatbots safely: clear owners, measurable controls, and evidence you can show a regulator. 2

Five Privacy Principles

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 3 · DATA P R I VA C Y Data privacy for chatbots: five principles Users share sensitive information in conversations. Every prompt, chat log, embedding and model-provider copy is a data store to protect. 1 Be transparent • Why data is collected • How it is used • How long it is kept • That users are talking to AI 2 Secure stored data • Strict, role-based access • Encryption in transit and at rest • Separate keys for chat logs 3 Minimize and de-identify • Collect only what's needed • Pseudonymize or anonymize • Differential privacy for analytics 4 Define disposal • Retention period per data type • Archive or delete on schedule • Honor deletion requests 5 Audit continuously • Access logs and reviews • Regular control testing • Evidence for regulators 8
Back to slide navigation

Slide 9 of 24

Privacy Action Items

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 3 · DATA P R I VA C Y Privacy action items: now and next Control What to do When Encryption Encrypt sensitive data in transit and at rest, including chat logs and vector stores Now Access control Limit user data to people who need it: role-based access and multi-factor authentication Now Data minimization Collect only the data the bot needs for its task; strip the rest before storage Now Auditing Audit systems, access and processes regularly to find and fix vulnerabilities Now PII redaction Detect and mask personal data in prompts, retrieved text and logs before it reaches the model Now Vendor terms Use provider settings and contracts with no training on your data and limited retention Now Pseudonymization Replace identifiers with tokens so the bot works without exposing who the user is Next Differential privacy Add calibrated noise when analyzing conversation data in aggregate Next 9

Protecting Identities

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 3 · DATA P R I VA C Y Three ways to protect identities in chat data Pseudonymization WHAT IT DOES Replaces identifiers (name, email) with tokens; a separate key can re-link them REVERSIBLE? Yes, with the key. Still personal data under GDPR BEST FOR Support bots that must look up a customer's account Anonymization WHAT IT DOES Removes or generalizes identifiers so people cannot be re-identified REVERSIBLE? No, if done well. Watch for re-identification from combined fields BEST FOR Sharing transcripts, training and testing data Differential privacy WHAT IT DOES Adds calibrated noise to results so no single person changes the outcome much REVERSIBLE? No. Gives a mathematical privacy guarantee BEST FOR Aggregate analytics and reporting on conversations 10

Slide 11 of 24

Differential Privacy

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 3 · DATA P R I VA C Y How differential privacy works Conversation data + noise Aggregate answer Example: “How many users asked about refunds this week?” returns 1,204 plus or minus a small random amount. The trend is clear, but no single user's question can be detected. Privacy budget (ε) Smaller ε: stronger privacy, noisier results Larger ε: more accurate, weaker privacy 1 Noise is added before analysis Differential privacy adds carefully calibrated noise to data or results before anyone analyzes them. 2 It balances privacy and utility The noise protects each individual while still allowing accurate analysis of the whole dataset. 3 Calibrate the amount Large enough to hide any one person's contribution; small enough not to distort the overall results. 11

Governed Bot Design

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 4 · B U I L D I N G G OV E R N E D B OT S Design considerations for LLM chatbots Knowledge and data • Use proprietary and up-to-date knowledge • Combine unstructured, structured and semi-structured sources • Choose how to split and chunk each source Retrieval and answers • Retrieve the right context for each question • Generate answers that cite their sources • Respect context-window limits; summarize long histories Cost and performance • Track token usage and cost per conversation • Set budgets, rate limits and timeouts • Route simple questions to smaller, cheaper models Every design choice is also a governance choice: it decides what the bot can see, say and spend. 12

Governed RAG Pipeline

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 4 · B U I L D I N G G OV E R N E D B OT S A governed RAG pipeline: controls at every step Documents CONTROL Classify sensitivity, scan for PII, approve sources Chunk and embed CONTROL Keep source and owner metadata; drop secrets Vector database CONTROL Encrypt; mirror the original document permissions Retrieve context CONTROL Filter by the user's access rights; log what was used LLM CONTROL Input guardrails: injection and PII checks; approved model only Response CONTROL Output guardrails: grounding, PII, toxicity; citations; human handoff Orchestration layer: applies constraints and changes on the input (before the model sees it) and on the output (before the user sees it), and logs every step. 13

Slide 14 of 24

Hallucination Controls

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 5 · R I S K C O N T R O L S Hallucination: confident but wrong Why it happens • Models predict plausible text, not verified facts • Missing, outdated or conflicting knowledge • Questions outside the bot's scope • Ambiguous prompts with no instruction to abstain Controls Ground answers in approved sources (RAG) Show citations users can check Let the bot say “I don't know” and hand off Check groundedness automatically before replying Keep prices, policies and legal terms on verified content Lesson from Air Canada Its chatbot misstated the bereavement-fare policy. The tribunal found the airline liable for negligent misrepresentation and ordered it to pay the difference. Your bot's answer is your company's answer. 14

Slide 15 of 24

Prompt Injection and Brittle Prompts

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 5 · R I S K C O N T R O L S Prompt injection and brittle prompts Prompt injection Instructions hidden in user input, or in retrieved documents, emails and web pages, override the bot's rules. CONTROLS • Treat retrieved content as data, never as instructions • Give tools least privilege; require approval for risky actions • Filter inputs and outputs; detect known attack patterns • Red-team regularly with new attack styles Brittle prompts Small changes to prompts, models or data shift behavior in ways nobody tested. CONTROLS • Version prompts like code, with reviews • Pin model versions; re-test before every upgrade • Keep a regression suite of real user questions • Roll changes out to a small share of traffic first 15

Poisoning and Supply Chain Risk

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 5 · R I S K C O N T R O L S Data poisoning and supply chain risk Where poisoning can happen Training and fine-tuning data Bad examples teach the model wrong or harmful behavior Knowledge base (RAG) documents A planted or edited page changes the bot's answers Vector store and agent memory Injected entries resurface in future conversations Controls ✓ Ingest only from approved, owned sources ✓ Review and sign content before indexing ✓ Track provenance: who added what, and when ✓ Detect anomalies; re-index from clean copies ✓ Vet models, datasets and plugins before use ✓ Keep an AI bill of materials for every bot 16

Governing Agents

Evaluation and Release Gates

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 5 · R I S K C O N T R O L S Evaluation: test before launch, monitor after Pre-launch • Golden question sets • Red teaming • Safety and privacy tests Release gate • Pass thresholds per metric • Sign-off by owner and risk • Documented results Production • Online checks on live traffic • User feedback and escalations • Drift alerts; periodic re-tests What to measure Groundedness Answer relevance Safety and toxicity PII leakage Injection resistance Task success Latency Cost per conversation Use LLM-as-judge for scale, and calibrate it against human reviewers. 18

Monitoring and Incident Response

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Chatbot Governance 0 7 · O P E R AT I N G M O D E L Monitoring and incident response What to log • Prompts and responses, with PII masked • Retrieved sources behind each answer • Tool calls and human approvals • Model and prompt versions in use • User feedback and escalations Keep logs only as long as your retention policy allows. Incident playbook 1 Detect Alerts, evaluation failures, user reports 2 Contain Kill switch or fall back to human agents 3 Fix Patch prompt, data or guardrail; re-test 4 Disclose Notify users or regulators where required 5 Learn Add the case to the regression suite 21

Key Takeaways

Key takeaways 1 Chatbots speak for your company: you own what they say and do. 2 Build privacy in: minimize, protect and dispose of conversation data. 3 Put controls at every step of the pipeline, and test before and after launch. 4 Name owners, follow recognized frameworks, and keep evidence regulators can check. 24

Frequently asked questions

What does chatbot governance cover?

The presentation connects accountability, privacy, security, answer quality, tool permissions, evaluation and incident response across the chatbot lifecycle.

Where does the deck place RAG controls?

It places checks at document intake, chunking and embedding, storage, retrieval, model input and response output, with orchestration and traceability across the pipeline.

How does governance change when a bot can act?

The deck adds scoped identities, least-privilege tools, approval for consequential actions, sandboxing, action logs and mechanisms to stop execution.

How is evaluation organized?

The presentation separates pre-launch tests, release gates and production monitoring. It includes groundedness, relevance, safety, privacy, injection resistance, task success, latency and cost.

Are the regulatory dates and rankings verified on this page?

No. The regulatory summaries, framework editions and risk rankings are reproduced from the supplied November 2026 deck. They are not independently verified legal guidance or a compliance determination.
